official.tuition_coverage_note: Full programme fees are covered by the fellowship.
benefits: Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation (the page states 'close to Oxford')
A monthly personal living allowance (stipend), confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Arrival allowance paid on arrival in the UK, and departure allowance where applicable to the fellowship type
A travel top-up allowance to attend events in London for those in receipt of non-London stipends
A contribution of up to GBP 75 for TB testing where required for the visa application
Reimbursement of the UK visa application fee for the fellow only
Reimbursement of the Immigration Health Surcharge, or a contribution towards travel insurance of up to GBP 200
A research allowance as a contribution towards producing a thesis/dissertation or conducting research associated with the programme, confirmed in the Final Award Letter
eligibility: Citizen of and resident in one of the listed European countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden or Switzerland
Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field)
At least five years' relevant professional experience (7,200 hours, calculated from weeks worked and hours per week; a working week comprises 35-60 hours and a working year 40-50 weeks)

Mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation
Working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy or operational effectiveness
Able to demonstrate leadership potential and commitment to applying the knowledge and networks gained within their organisation and/or country on completion

General Chevening Fellowship criteria: citizen of a fellowship-eligible country or territory, potential to rise to leadership and influence, return to the country of award for at least one year after the fellowship ends
Residents of European overseas territories may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which they are a citizen
requirements: Meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria and all programme-specific requirements
Apply through the Chevening online application system reached from the relevant European country/territory page

Demonstrate five years' (7,200 hours) of relevant professional experience using the published calculation method; the experience need not be in one period of employment - up to fifteen employment periods can be submitted

Ensure the employing organisation will release you for the six-week programme - the page states it is the applicant's responsibility and that neither the British embassy/high commission nor the Chevening Secretariat can intervene
Secure and comply with UK entry clearance (visa) requirements including medical clearance
On return of the acceptance form, agree to abide by the Chevening Fellowship terms and conditions for the duration of the award
documents: The completed Chevening Fellowship application form submitted through the online application system
Return of the award acceptance form after selection, on which the terms and conditions are accepted
Medical clearance for UK entry clearance - the award is contingent on the Fellow's ability to procure the visa and receive medical clearance

The Final Award Letter (FAL), which confirms all financial elements of the award, the stipend amount, tenure dates, and whether accommodation, a research allowance, arrival and departure allowances apply
Any compulsory documentation requested by the Secretariat during the award - failure to return it can lead to stipend suspension
selection_criteria: Assessment against the general Chevening Fellowship criteria plus the published programme-specific requirements, and against the needs of a cohort drawn from the listed European countries

Chevening Fellowship objectives include supporting mid-career professionals in positions of leadership and influence, offering training and professional development relevant to UK international strategic priorities, increasing the breadth and diversity of Chevening awards, and supporting FCDO foreign policy priorities
Applicants shortlisted in the selection process are invited to group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference
coverage: Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship including pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford
Monthly personal living allowance (stipend) confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Visa fee reimbursement for the fellow, Immigration Health Surcharge reimbursement or up to GBP 200 towards travel insurance, and up to GBP 75 towards required TB testing
application_method: Confirm citizenship and residence in one of the 35 listed European countries and that the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria are met
Check the five-year (7,200 hour) work experience total using the published calculation method before submitting
Apply through the Chevening online application system reached from the 'apply today' link for your country/territory
Answer the eligibility questions and complete each section of the form, including employment history and research interests
Attend any selection or interview stage notified by Chevening or the local Chevening team
On offer, return the acceptance form to accept the terms and conditions
Attend the pre-departure briefing hosted by the British embassy or high commission before travelling, and the welcome reception/induction on arrival in the UK
official.application_route: Online through the Chevening application system reached from your country/territory page, with work experience entered as employment periods and interviews conducted in French or English.

official.description: The Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship, delivered by Cranfield University, is a six-week Chevening Fellowship for mid-career professionals who are citizens and residents of 35 listed European countries and who work in defence, security and related fields. The fellowship covers full programme fees, living expenses with pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford, return economy airfare, a monthly personal living allowance and related allowances.

applicant_utility.summary: The hard filter here is citizenship plus residence: you must be a citizen of and resident in one of 35 listed European countries at the point of application, hold a postgraduate qualification, and clear the 7,200-hour (five-year) work-experience bar, which the online system calculates from the weeks and hours you enter. Applications close at 11:00 UTC on 12 October 2026, so with days left the priority is a complete employment history and a clear articulation of how your role influences organisational capability, policy, strategy or operational effectiveness. The award is genuinely comprehensive - fees, accommodation close to Oxford, return airfare, stipend, visa and health surcharge - but it is calculated for the fellow alone: there are no dependant provisions and Chevening strongly advises against bringing family.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career defence, security, law-enforcement, intelligence, civil-protection or international-organisation professionals from the 35 eligible European countries with five-plus years of relevant experience and a postgraduate qualification.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are both a citizen of and resident in one of the 35 listed countries as at application
Total your work experience using the published method (weeks x hours, 35-60 hour weeks, 40-50 week years) and confirm you clear 7,200 hours; remember up to fifteen employment periods can be entered
Secure your employer's agreement to release you for the full six-week programme before applying - Chevening cannot intervene
Prepare to interview in French or English per your preference if shortlisted
common_rejection_risks: Being a citizen but not a resident (or vice versa) of a listed country at application
Falling short of 7,200 hours because employment periods were entered incompletely or with inconsistent hours
Applying without the employer's release, which the page makes the applicant's sole responsibility
Describing a role without influence potential over organisational capability, policy, strategy or operational effectiveness
Planning to bring dependants - the award supports fellow costs only and dependants' visas are not endorsed or funded
Assuming deferral is possible - deferrals are granted only in the case of pregnancy, and extensions are exceptional and capped at 12 months
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The fellowship covers programme fees, accommodation close to Oxford, living expenses, return airfare and the standard allowances; anything beyond that - personal spending, family costs, or expenses outside the covered allowances - is the fellow's own.
document_audit: The Final Award Letter is the authoritative document for every financial element - stipend, tenure, accommodation and allowances - so read it before committing
Medical clearance and UK entry clearance are conditions of the award; the up-to-GBP 75 TB testing contribution only helps where TB testing is required for the visa
Acceptance is only effective on return of the acceptance form, which binds you to the terms and conditions
Failure to return compulsory documentation requested during the award can suspend the stipend
alerts: The award is contingent on procuring UK entry clearance and receiving medical clearance
There is a two-year return-home expectation built into Chevening terms and a general one-year minimum for fellowships after completion - plan your employer's expectations accordingly
Fellows must not be outside the UK for more than 30 days in total during the award, must not take other publicly funded awards, and need approval for any part-time work outside the programme
Because chevening.org could not be re-fetched on the verification date, re-confirm the deadline and cohort dates on the official page immediately
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online Chevening application from your country page with eligibility questions, employment history and research interests; shortlisted candidates attend group meetings and interviews in French or English; selection triggers the Final Award Letter and the acceptance form, followed by pre-departure briefing and January/March 2027 cohort attendance.
